summary.p: A complete copy of the Táríkh-i-'Álam-árá-yi-'Abbásí, a very detailed history of Sháh 'Abbás the Great, compiled by Iskandar Munshí in 1025/1616, in two volumes, not uniform. For particulars of the work, see Rieu's Persian Catalogue, pp. 185-188, etc.

Vol. 1 (H. 13) contains twelve preliminary Discourses (Maqálát), followed by the first Sahífa, describing the course of events down to the accession of Shah 'Abbás the Great (reigned A.H. 996-1038=A.D. 1588-1629). The chief contents are:

INTRODUCTION (MUQADDAMA) comprising 12 Discourses (Maqála) as follows: Maqála i (f. 6). Genealogy and ancestors of Shah 'Abbás (Shaykh Ṣafiyyu'd-Dín, f. 12"; Ṣadru'd-Din, f. 14; Sháh Ismá'íl, f. 24"; Sháh Tahmásp, f. 45'; Shah Muḥammad Khudá-banda, f. 104).
Maqála ii (f. 106). Piety and devoutness of Sháh 'Abbás.
Maqála iii (f. 106). His wisdom, knowledge, and state-craft.
Maqála iv (f. 107). His escapes from many perils and his worthiness to be entitled Ṣáḥib-qirán, or "Lord of a fortunate planetary conjunction."
Maqála v (f. 108). His well-considered measures to increase public security and the happiness of his subjects.

Maqála vii (f. 110*), viii (f. 110), ix (f. 110), x (f. 111), xi (f. 111), xii (f. 113): his rules of government and maxims of administration; his simplicity and informality in private life; his consideration for his attendants and dislike of flattery; his knowledge of men and their characters; his charitable bequests and pious foundations; his wars and victories.

PART I [FIRST SAHIFA] contains the history of Sháh 'Abbás from his birth at Herát on Ramaḍán 1, 978 (Jan. 27, 1571), or Ramaḍán 1, 979 (Jan. 17, 1572), until his accession. Some of the principal topics are: the birth and childhood of Shah Abbás (f. 114); children and grandchildren of Sháh Tahmásp (f. 118); notable men of his reign, including Amirs (f. 119), Sayyids and 'Ulamá (f. 120), Ministers (f. 129), physicians (f. 132), calligraphists (f. 134"), painters and illuminators (f. 136), poets (f. 138), singers and minstrels (f. 144'); detailed and connected history of the Safawis from the murder of Haydar Mírzá (in 984/1576) and accession of Shah Ismá'íl II (ff. 145' et seqq.) to the murder of Hamza Mírzá (994/1586) and accession of his brother Sháh 'Abbás in the following year.

This MS., transcribed in 1095/1684, comprises 279 ff. of 37.2 x 16.5 c. and 19 ll., and is written in a small, neat ta'liq with rubrications. It once formed part of the library of Muḥammad Ḥasan Khán Ṣaná'd-Dawla, whose book-plate it bears.

revisionDesc.change: Claude (auto-merge) Merged manual/ai/multi_match/H_13_14.xml (one AI file describing both volumes, whose generic physDesc block wrongly gave a combined folio count for both volumes together under a single objectDesc) into this record. The prose clearly separates the two volumes by class-mark ("Vol. 1 (H. 13)"/"Vol. II (H. 14)") and gives distinct physical stats for each, so those per-volume figures were used instead of the generic block. Completed objectDesc/@form (was "other") and supportDesc/@material (was "chart") from the AI source; added layoutDesc/@writtenLines="19"; added handNote script/description; added a provenance element naming the manuscript's earlier owner, Muḥammad Ḥasan Khán Ṣaná'd-Dawla (no authority key available). Not yet reviewed by a cataloguer.
